title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 4th District
area: Northwest and parts of northeast Louisiana, including Shreveport.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026. If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map.

candidates.name: Mike Johnson
candidates.currentRole: Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives; U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 4th District (since 2017)

priorities.text: Lists reducing federal debt and spending, entitlement reform, and "pro-growth tax reforms and permanent tax reductions" as priorities under a platform of fiscal responsibility.
Says maintaining U.S. military strength, including investment in "air, land, sea, nuclear and cyber warfare," is a governing priority.

positions.summary: Touted a year of sustained immigration enforcement, including hundreds of thousands of deportations and increased border-security resources, as a governing achievement.
positions.quote: Sustained deterrence and enforcement have held for a full year: Border crossings down 93% year-over-year . For seven consecutive months, from May to November, ZERO illegal aliens were released into the country.

positions.summary: Described the SAVE Act as requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections and said House Republicans are working to get the SAVE America Act to the President.
positions.quote: the SAVE Act just simply says, you must have proof of citizenship if you're going to register to vote in federal elections

positions.summary: Called the President's tariffs an effective tool and said Congress should not step in the middle of them.
positions.quote: The tariffs have been a tool that the President has used very effectively to level the playing field and put America back on top.

record.text: Serves as Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives (since October 2023), responsible for setting the chamber's legislative agenda.

Previously chaired the House Republican Study Committee and the Judiciary Committee's Subcommittee on the Constitution and Limited Government, and served as Vice Chairman of the House Republican Conference.

priorities.text: Supports Medicare for All, saying "healthcare should depend on need, not income," citing the number of Americans without health coverage.
priorities.quote: It is time for change. Medicare for All ensures everyone can see a doctor, get medicine, and stay healthy without going into debt or skipping care. Healthcare should depend on need, not income.

priorities.text: Warns that federal cuts threaten to worsen food insecurity, noting more than 800,000 people in Louisiana, including nearly 250,000 children, live with food insecurity.
Wants to overturn Citizens United, saying big money has too much influence in politics and corporate interests are put ahead of working families.
priorities.quote: We must overturn Citizens United and stop dark money from controlling politics. Elections should be about the people, not the richest donors.

positions.summary: Supports a Medicare for All system so healthcare depends on need rather than income.
positions.quote: Medicare for All ensures everyone can see a doctor, get medicine, and stay healthy without going into debt or skipping care.

priorities.text: Wants to reduce the cost of groceries, healthcare and childcare by expanding tax credits and "holding corporations accountable for price gouging," and to cap insurance rate hikes.
Supports expanding access to universal pre-K for 3- and 4-year-olds and guaranteeing free school lunches for every student.
priorities.quote: Guarantee free school lunches for every student in America — because no child should be hungry in the classroom.

priorities.text: Wants to reevaluate spending abroad and redirect federal resources toward domestic needs like schools, childcare and small-business growth.

statements.quote: Expand access to universal pre-K for all 3- and 4-year-olds, funded by smarter budgeting of existing federal expenditures.
statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.name: Gordon Heslop

priorities.text: Says the prosperity of the middle class is essential to the economy.
priorities.quote: I view the prosperity of the middle class as essential to a strong American economy and will constantly push for measures to address their problems and enhance their well-being.

priorities.text: Says he will support the rural economy and opposes rural hospital closures.
priorities.quote: I will be a strong supporter of the rural economy.

priorities.text: Lists the everyday level of prices, affordable housing, medical services, education, the rural economy and foreign policy as the areas of public policy he is passionate about.
priorities.quote: The everyday level of prices, affordable housing, medical services, education, the rural economy, and foreign policy.

positions.summary: Says he opposed the President's tariff policies and proposes abolishing the tariffs, citing higher costs for consumers and farmers.
positions.quote: One such example is abolishing the tariffs which increase costs for everyone and hit our farmers double

positions.summary: Says he will support government programs for medical care, proposing coverage for children's doctor visits, prescriptions and dental care, preventive screenings, and pregnancy care.
positions.quote: I will support some government programs to help with medical care.

researchNotes: Checked Speaker Johnson's official issues pages (Individual Freedom, Limited Government, Rule of Law, Peace through Strength, Fiscal Responsibility, Free Markets, Human Dignity) and several press releases; most describe general conservative principles rather than statements matching specific ISSUES substance, so positions are limited to the two where his site directly addressed the issue (immigration enforcement, abortion). No statements found addressing gun laws, tariffs, climate transition pace, or Israel aid specifically enough to meet the research standard. Gordon Heslop's items come from his Louisiana-race Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (he also ran in Texas and Missouri primaries; responses to those races are not used). No campaign website or public statements were found for Mike Nichols. Gordon Heslop's biography draws on his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; Mike Nichols has not completed Ballotpedia's survey, and his biography is limited to the BallotReady profile because his campaign website did not load.
